name: Dream Factories: The Studios Behind the Screen
description: Paramount, Warner, MGM, UFA, Disney, Toho and Ghibli: the film companies that built the studio system, and the films that made them.

checkpoints.name: Studios take shape
checkpoints.note: Paramount began in 1912 and Berlin's UFA in 1917; German cinema produced The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari in 1920. In 1923 Walt Disney and his brother began a cartoon company and the Warner brothers formed Warner Bros., and in 1924 Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer was formed by a merger.

checkpoints.name: Sound and the studio system
checkpoints.note: The Jazz Singer of 1927, from Warner Bros., helped bring spoken dialogue to film, and UFA made Metropolis. Mickey Mouse and RKO appeared in 1928 and Toho in 1932. Disney's Snow White came in 1937, MGM's The Wizard of Oz in 1939, and RKO's Citizen Kane in 1941.

checkpoints.name: War and decline
checkpoints.note: Warner Bros. made Casablanca in 1942, and UFA ended with the war in 1945. A 1948 court ruling forced the big US studios to sell their cinemas. Toho released Godzilla and Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai in 1954, and RKO closed in 1959.

checkpoints.name: A new age of animation
checkpoints.note: Walt Disney died in 1966. Studio Ghibli was founded in 1985, and Disney's The Lion King came in 1994. Toy Story of 1995, made by Pixar with Disney, was a computer-animated feature, and Ghibli's Spirited Away of 2001 won wide praise.
